sections.heading: Section – A : OBSERVATION AND REPORTING  ( 15 marks )

blocks.instruction: Fill in the gaps with the correct answer. ( 6 x 1 = 6  )
blocks.notes: Each item gives two choices in brackets, e.g. '( Kerala / Karnataka )' (effectively 2-option choice). (a) Ugadi Pachadi: textbook p.73 says Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telengana, so Karnataka. (c) choice bracket wraps over two lines: '( Energy Giving / Body-Building )'. (d) uses curly quotes ‘No’.
Answer slot is '(          )' after each statement. (b) Idli is steamed -> False; (e) False.

blocks.instruction: Write a short note on the following. ( 2 x 2 = 4  )
blocks.notes: (a) 'Importance of water in our diet.' (b) 'Balanced food' (no full stop). 4 answer lines each. Judgement items: need rubrics.

sections.heading: Section – B : IDENTIFICATION AND CLASSIFICATION  ( 12 marks )

blocks.notes: TYPO kept: (a) 'What did Surabhi’s grandmother use to eat to during summers and winters?' ('use to eat to' — stray 'to'; textbook spells the name 'Surbhi'). Answer from textbook p.74: jowar and bajra roti in winters, jau roti in summers. (e) 'Who is a ‘Chef’?' — its 3 answer lines run onto page 3. Short-answer questions sit in a section headed IDENTIFICATION AND CLASSIFICATION (as printed).

Two-column table 'Protective Foods' | 'Energy Giving Foods' with one empty row. Printed as 2 x 1 — interpretation: one point for each column (what each food type does). Instruction ends 'between.' with nothing after (the table supplies the terms). Judgement item.

blocks.instruction: Give an example of the ingredients or food items that match each of the tastes listed below? ( 6 x ½ = 3 )
blocks.notes: Imperative instruction ends with '?' as printed. Six-column table: Sweet | Sour | Salty | Pungent | Bitter | Astringent, one empty row. Open answers — need wide acceptable lists.

blocks.instruction: Draw any two junk food and also write the names. ( 2 x 1 = 2 )

pictures.what: two empty boxes side by side, each with a short name line at the top

blocks.notes: Grammar as printed ('two junk food'). Drawing task — child draws; in the app likely name + description/self-check; rubric needed.

sections.heading: Section – C :  DISCOVERY OF FACTS ( 13 marks )

blocks.notes: Each item has two blanks (½ per name implied). Items: a. Food items which can be eaten without cooking; b. Water – rich fruits (spaced en dash as printed); c. Food groups; d. Food items in the stall of super food (textbook p.74: millet foods — jowar upma, jowar/bajra roti, jau roti); e. Meals of the day.

Left: a. Boiling b. Steaming c. Frying d. Roasting e. Grilling f. Baking. Right (with '(      )' slots): cakes, rice, popcorn, idiyappam, puri, chicken. Marks bracket '( 6 x ½ = 3)' has no space before ')'. Intended: Boiling–rice, Steaming–idiyappam, Frying–puri, Roasting–popcorn, Grilling–chicken, Baking–cakes. Roasting/Grilling vs popcorn/chicken is debatable (chicken can be roasted) — accept both readings.

blocks.instruction: Circle the odd one out. ( 4 x ½ = 2 )
blocks.notes: Printed '10.Circle' with no space after the number. Each item ends with an italic clue in brackets naming the group the OTHER four belong to, e.g. '( Clue: Energy-Giving Food )'. Expected: a. lemon, b. tomato, c. cheese, d. pizza. (a) potato is a tuber, still energy-giving; fine.

blocks.instruction: Locate the following states in the given map. ( 3 x 1 = 3 )

pictures.what: outline political map of India with state boundaries and no names, in a heavy black frame; the child must mark a. Andhra Pradesh, b. Karnataka, c. Telangana

blocks.notes: Item line printed in bold: 'a. Andhra Pradesh , b. Karnataka , c. Telangana'. Links to Ugadi Pachadi states. Must be drawn as an SVG India map with numbered/selectable southern states (at least AP, Karnataka, Telangana plus neighbours as distractors). Not in the textbook as a map task — beyond-textbook skill.
